correctness.rationale: For q in (0,1), λ,ℓ,c>0 the two action payoffs give G(p)=ℓ(e^{-λq m(p)}-e^{-λ m(p)})-c with m(p)=1-(1-q)p. Differentiating H shows unique strict maximum at m*=ln(1/q)/(λ(1-q)); q<m*<1 is exactly the strict λ interval. A horizontal cost level intersects both monotonic branches precisely when above H(q) and H(1), below H(m*). The resulting G signs are (-,+,-), giving precisely p0 and interior roots as pure/mixed Nash and the claimed one-dimensional replicator stabilities, excluding p=1. At equality/tangency one cannot infer two distinct interior fractions. The exact q=1/2,λ=2,c/ℓ=63/256 factorization y-y²-c=-(y-7/16)(y-9/16) produces p-=0.34664285 and p+=0.84927171. Independently verified rational identity, window, endpoint and interior signs.
residual_risks: Applies to a fixed exogenous Poisson exposure horizon, continuum agents and expected payoffs; does not prove claims for an evolving epidemic or finite-population dynamics.

value.rationale: The exact bistability window is a substantively motivated boundary between two local adoption attractors produced solely by infection-probability saturation. It identifies an explicit stable all-unmasked state coexisting with partial masking, establishes necessary and sufficient parameter inequalities and a rationally certified witness. The distinction from the linear infection-rate approximation changes qualitative equilibrium predictions and is mathematically useful for game-model comparison without requiring empirical public-health claims.
residual_risks: Biological interpretation depends on frozen prevalence, well-mixed continuum and expected-payoff replicator dynamics; no real-world adoption prediction is established.

limitations: Only symmetric Nash mix and the specified replicator adjustment, not actual epidemic dynamics.
